therapeutic_hypothesis.claimed_target: P6 (Neiguan) acupressure point / peripheral nerve afferents at the wrist
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: suppression of nausea and vomiting reflex
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: patients undergoing cesarean section under regional anesthesia
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: incidence of nausea and vomiting during the surgical procedure

results.effect_size: Nausea: control 44, metoclopramide+ondansetron 14, P6 22 participants; Vomiting: control 27, metoclopramide+ondansetron 10, P6 8 participants
subgroup_findings: P6 stimulator vs control for nausea: p=0.00005 (significant); P6 vs metoclopramide+ondansetron: p=0.1 (not significant)
P6 stimulator vs control for vomiting: p=0.0002 (significant); P6 vs metoclopramide+ondansetron: p=0.8 (not significant)
Metoclopramide+ondansetron vs control for nausea: p<0.00001 (significant)
Metoclopramide+ondansetron vs control for vomiting: p=0.001 (significant)
Stage I nausea: P6 vs control p=0.0004 (significant); P6 vs metoclopramide+ondansetron p=0.09 (not significant)
Stage I vomiting: P6 vs control p=0.0004 (significant); P6 vs metoclopramide+ondansetron p=1 (not significant)
Satisfaction of anti-emetic treatment: metoclopramide+ondansetron vs control p=0.02 (significant); P6 vs control p=0.2 (not significant)

dose_info.dose: Metoclopramide 10 mg IV; Ondansetron 8 mg IV; P6 stimulator at comfortable level
dose_info.schedule: single dose immediately prior to regional anesthesia; P6 continuous during procedure

context.indication: nausea and vomiting during cesarean section under regional anesthesia
context.duration: duration of cesarean section surgical procedure
